episode_title: What Happens When You See What Others Don't? with Melissa Voss
question: What problem did Melissa Voss identify in the accounting industry that led to founding Fuseworks?
transcript_excerpt: Melissa worked with Scott, her co-founder, at an accounting firm and uncovered that accountants were doing many tasks repetitively that could be automated. They realized there were smart ways to remove the parts of the job that robots could do, leaving humans to do the human parts of their job. They developed internal solutions over several years, and after getting requests from other firms to use their technology, they decided to productize and commercialize what they had built.

episode_title: What Happens When You See What Others Don't? with Melissa Voss
question: How did Melissa Voss build a high-engagement workplace culture at Fuseworks achieving 96% employee satisfaction?
transcript_excerpt: Melissa deliberately focused on getting the right people in the right seats with aligned values from the start. She prioritizes people first, knowing that if you have the right people, everything else follows. She implemented intentional practices including: giving employees Friday afternoons off for free, taking the whole team on retreats to celebrate milestones and plan together, being very intentional about leadership support, and involving the team in business goals and rewards. She emphasizes caring about people, not just driving profits.

episode_title: What Happens When You See What Others Don't? with Melissa Voss
question: What changes did Melissa Voss make to lead remote UK teams across time zones?
transcript_excerpt: Melissa made an intentional business decision to expand to the UK as their first international market because it was aligned with their Australian operations. To lead the remote team, she restructures her week to give herself time and freedom to show up as her best self during evening calls. She starts each week with a call to the UK team to share highlights from the previous week and discuss wins. She also travels to the UK once or twice a year to spend a block of time with the team in person, focusing on understanding their challenges rather than just process management.

episode_title: What Happens When You See What Others Don't? with Melissa Voss
question: What percentage of Fuseworks development team is female and what does Melissa Voss think about women in technology?
transcript_excerpt: Fuseworks has about a third of its development team as female, including current interns. Melissa believes women bring completely different viewpoints and perspectives to the work. She emphasizes that emotional intelligence, the ability to juggle multiple responsibilities, and diverse approaches are strengths that women bring. She encourages women to embrace their natural way of doing things rather than apologizing for it, noting that she has never doubted her ability to bring value to the table as a leader.

episode_title: What Happens When You See What Others Don't? with Melissa Voss
question: What has been the most important factor in Fuseworks' business success according to Melissa Voss?
transcript_excerpt: Building relationships and partnerships has been the biggest success factor for Melissa. She has 150% embraced every relationship, opportunity, and partnership with software providers, industry people, and clients. Many client relationships have turned into friendships. She believes the business has a great, trusted, respected brand because they are nice people with good relationships fundamentally, and this approach is mirrored by her team in how they win business and support clients.
